topic: Agencies report 'brief bloat' from AI-written client briefs: M&C Saatchi North America CEO estimates 85% of client briefs are AI-written; Basis survey 56.4% use AI to build briefs (Digiday, 5 Nov 2026)
instagram_caption:
AI is writing your briefs. Agencies say it shows.

Digiday reported on 5 November that agencies are seeing "brief bloat": client briefs drafted with AI that read polished but run long and miss a clear goal. M&C Saatchi's North America CEO estimates 85% of the client briefs her agency now receives are written with AI tools. Some run to hundreds of pages. A Basis Technologies survey found 56.4% of marketers and agencies use AI to build strategy, media or creative briefs.

Why it matters: a brief is where a team decides what it is trying to achieve. When AI writes it before anyone has done that thinking, every campaign after it inherits the fog.

What to do this week:
1. Write the goal, the audience and the single message yourself, in five lines or fewer, before you open any AI tool.
2. Use AI to challenge the brief, not draft it. Ask it for gaps, risks and counter-arguments.
3. Cap briefs at two pages and check every number in them against its source.

AI can polish a brief. It can't decide what you want.

AI is writing your briefs. Agencies say it shows.

Digiday reported on 5 November that agencies are dealing with "brief bloat": client briefs drafted with AI that read polished but run long, lean on jargon and lack a clear marketing goal. M&C Saatchi's North America CEO estimates that 85% of the client briefs her agency now receives are written with AI tools, and some briefs run to hundreds of pages. A Basis Technologies survey found that 56.4% of marketers and agencies now use AI to build strategy, media or creative briefs.

Our view: the brief is where a team decides what it is trying to achieve. When AI produces the document before anyone has done that thinking, every campaign that follows inherits the lack of clarity, and agencies spend their first week decoding instead of creating.

Three steps worth taking this week:
1. Write the goal, the audience and the single message yourself, in five lines or fewer, before opening any AI tool.
2. Use AI to challenge the brief rather than draft it: ask it for gaps, risks and counter-arguments.
3. Cap briefs at two pages and check every number against its source.

AI can polish a brief. It cannot decide what you want.
